stem: Two squares of side 6 cm overlap in a 2 cm × 2 cm region. What is the total visible area?
visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 280 180' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='280' height='180' fill='#f9f9f9' rx='8'/><rect x='30' y='30' width='120' height='120' fill='#3498db' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='#3498db' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='110' y='80' width='120' height='120' fill='#e74c3c' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='#e74c3c' stroke-width='2' transform='translate(0,-50)'/><rect x='110' y='30' width='40' height='40' fill='#9b59b6' fill-opacity='0.4' stroke='#9b59b6' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='123' y='55' font-size='11' fill='#9b59b6'>2×2</text><text x='60' y='100' font-size='13' fill='#3498db'>6 cm</text><text x='175' y='80' font-size='13' fill='#e74c3c'>6 cm</text></svg>
solution:
Step 1: Area of each square = 6 × 6 = 36 cm².
Step 2: Total area if we add both = 36 + 36 = 72 cm².
Step 3: The overlapping region (2 × 2 = 4 cm²) is counted twice.
Step 4: Total visible area = 72 − 4 = 68 cm².
Answer: 68 cm².

stem: Two circles each have radius 5 cm. They overlap such that the overlapping region has area 10 cm². What is the total area covered by both circles? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
solution:
Step 1: Area of each circle = π × 5² = 25π ≈ 78.5 cm².
Step 2: Total covered area = 78.5 + 78.5 − 10 = 147 cm².
Using inclusion-exclusion: total = area₁ + area₂ − overlap = 78.5 + 78.5 − 10 = 147 cm².
Answer: 147 cm².

stem: In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC where D is on AB and E is on AC. If AD = 4, DB = 6, and BC = 15, what is DE?
visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 260 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='260' height='200' fill='#f9f9f9' rx='8'/><polygon points='130,20 20,180 240,180' fill='none' stroke='#3498db' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='86' y1='84' x2='174' y2='84' stroke='#e74c3c' stroke-width='2'/><text x='100' y='45' font-size='11' fill='#333'>4</text><text x='70' y='130' font-size='11' fill='#333'>6</text><text x='125' y='195' font-size='11' fill='#333'>15</text><text x='60' y='80' font-size='11' fill='#e74c3c'>D</text><text x='178' y='80' font-size='11' fill='#e74c3c'>E</text><text x='128' y='15' font-size='11' fill='#333'>A</text><text x='8' y='192' font-size='11' fill='#333'>B</text><text x='238' y='192' font-size='11' fill='#333'>C</text></svg>
solution:
Step 1: Since DE ∥ BC, triangles ADE and ABC are similar.
Step 2: AD/AB = 4/(4+6) = 4/10 = 2/5.
Step 3: DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/5.
Step 4: DE = (2/5) × 15 = 6.
Answer: 6.

stem: In a right triangle, the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse creates two smaller triangles. Are these smaller triangles similar to each other and to the original?
visual_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 200 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="30,30 30,170 170,170" fill="none" stroke="#7B1FA2" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="30" y1="170" x2="82" y2="82" stroke="#7B1FA2" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5,3"/><text x="20" y="25" font-size="14" fill="#333">A</text><text x="18" y="180" font-size="14" fill="#333">B</text><text x="175" y="180" font-size="14" fill="#333">C</text><text x="70" y="78" font-size="12" fill="#666">D</text><rect x="30" y="155" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="#7B1FA2" stroke-width="1"/></svg>

Step 1: Let the right angle be at B, and the altitude from B meets hypotenuse AC at D.
Step 2: Triangle ABD has angles: ∠ADB = 90°, ∠A, and ∠ABD = 90° − ∠A.
Step 3: Triangle BDC has angles: ∠BDC = 90°, ∠C = 90° − ∠A, and ∠DBC = ∠A.
Step 4: Original triangle ABC has angles: ∠B = 90°, ∠A, ∠C.
Step 5: All three triangles have the same set of angles, so all three are similar.
Answer: A) Yes, all three are similar.

solution:
Step 1: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.
Step 2: Half-chord = 24/2 = 12 cm.

Step 4: By the Pythagorean theorem: r² = 12² + 5² = 144 + 25 = 169.
Step 5: r = √169 = 13 cm.
Answer: 13 cm.
